query: Vertical lift modules (VLMs), vertical carousels and automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS) used in laboratories, biobanks, hospital and central-fill pharmacies, clean rooms and research facilities: what is stored (samples, consumables, reagents, tools, instruments), measured tray or carrier access times and picks per hour, reported benefits with numbers (floor space saved, pick accuracy, inventory traceability, ergonomics, access control), and reported problems (downtime, maintenance, being a single point of failure, what happens when the machine faults with items inside). Which of the reported benefits come from storing many passive items densely, and would any apply to a small number of instruments that run in place?
